title: Queue Control Exchange
description: Structural schema companion for contract: durable-queue/v0. One request or response line of the wire binding (line-delimited JSON over stdio or a local socket). Requests are discriminated by op with closed typed params. Responses echo op and carry a typed result or a typed error. Unknown ops fail closed with unknown_op. Daemon deployments require token on every request; harness stdio mode may omit it. replay and a tolerant conformance mode are deferred and absent from this vocabulary.

params.description: Children are enqueued to the parent's queue. Cross-queue fan-out is deferred.

consistent_cut.description: true when the last returned seq is a consistent cut (no later event has group <= it).

lease.description: A lease is a value. The queue is bound into it; the broker checks queue, message and token together on every lease operation.

leaseOutcome.description: stale_lease covers wrong token, wrong queue, expired or superseded lease. It is an outcome, not an error.

receiptOutcome.description: deduplicated: same key, same payload digest, within the window; message_id is the original. conflict: same key, different payload digest, within the window; nothing was accepted and message_id is the original.

idempotency_key.description: Producer-chosen. Scope is the queue. Lifetime is the backend's declared idempotency window measured from the original enqueued event, independent of message state.

payload_contract.description: Host-less capability token naming the payload's own contract. Carried, never validated by the broker.

payload.description: Opaque JSON payload within the I-JSON domain (RFC 7493: finite binary64-representable numbers, unique member names, well-formed Unicode) so that an RFC 8785 identity digest exists. A payload outside that domain is rejected at enqueue with invalid_params. Semantics are validated by the consumer against payload_contract, never by the broker.

payload_ref.description: Reference to an immutable body held as a contract: data-artifact/v0 artifact. Requires capability payload_ref. Tokens only; never a filesystem path.

newMessage.description: Producer input to enqueue and fan_out. Carries no broker-assigned fields.

id.description: Broker-assigned, unique per queue for the life of the ledger.

idempotency_key.description: Producer-chosen. Scope is the queue. Lifetime is the backend's declared idempotency window measured from the original enqueued event, independent of message state.

payload_contract.description: Host-less capability token naming the payload's own contract. Carried, never validated by the broker.

payload.description: Opaque JSON payload within the I-JSON domain (RFC 7493: finite binary64-representable numbers, unique member names, well-formed Unicode) so that an RFC 8785 identity digest exists. A payload outside that domain is rejected at enqueue with invalid_params. Semantics are validated by the consumer against payload_contract, never by the broker.

payload_ref.description: Reference to an immutable body held as a contract: data-artifact/v0 artifact. Requires capability payload_ref. Tokens only; never a filesystem path.

storedMessage.description: Mirror of queue-message.schema.json; controls assert the two stay identical.

artifactRef.description: Reference to an immutable body held as a contract: data-artifact/v0 artifact. Requires capability payload_ref. Tokens only; never a filesystem path.

ledgerEvent.description: Mirror of ledger-event.schema.json; controls assert the two stay identical.

group.description: seq of the first event in this event's atomic group; equals seq for a single-event step.

type.description: Closed vocabulary. Unknown types are rejected.

payload_digest.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical bytes of the message identity object: {"payload_contract": ..., "payload": ...} or {"payload_contract": ..., "payload_ref": {"artifact_id": ..., "digest": ...}}. Scheduling fields (not_before, expires_at, max_attempts, priority, ordering_key, attributes, trace) are not bound; on a repeated key the original wins.

group_size.description: Number of events in this event's atomic group. A prefix ending at seq N is a consistent cut iff, for the event at N, N - group + 1 == group_size.

capabilityProfile.description: Mirror of capability-profile.schema.json; controls assert the two stay identical.

conformance.description: deterministic: virtual clock, recorded ledger, exact normalized ledger match on every core vector. benchmark_only: the backend was exercised for measurement and makes no conformance claim. A tolerant wall-clock mode is deferred and not advertised in v0.

ledger.description: recorded: every transition appends its events in the same atomic step. inferred: reconstructed by an adapter; not an authoritative history and not admissible for deterministic conformance.

idempotency_window_ms.description: Required. Keyed deduplication is core; this is how long a key is live from the original enqueued event.

failure_model.description: The strongest failure an acknowledged enqueue or fan_out survives, as a guarantee. Independent of how the commit is implemented.

commit_strategy.description: Informational only (for example fsync-each-commit, group-commit-5ms, aof-everysec). Never upgrades failure_model.
